name: Caliphate City of Medina Azahara
description: Medina Azahara is the ruined palace-city that Caliph Abd ar-Rahman III began building near Córdoba, Spain, around 936–940 to show off his power. Its ceremonial halls, gardens, mosque and aqueduct-fed baths were sacked in a civil war about 70 years later and then forgotten. Only about a tenth of the 112-hectare site has been excavated, yet it already reveals the main palaces.
